title: How this draft was checked
body: drafter wrote the page from the blueprint you approved in batch 3. A fresh fact-checker read 84 claims against the code: 81 held and 3 were imprecise. It also type-checked the code blocks and ran the example through the real `createRenderer`. The register editor's 21 findings, 4 of them blocking, were applied. Four rechecks followed, and each finding is fixed.

The example's markdown and HTML blocks were regenerated with `serializeComponent` and `createRenderer` after every change, never retyped, and they match the renderer byte for byte. Each claim change was carried back to the blueprint.

title: Check the public render through a share link?
body: Your approved blueprint ends the verify procedure by publishing an entry and checking the published page. As drafted, that step couldn't be finished. The dev server runs the dev backend, so a publish never leaves the machine, and the component's code has to deploy before a public page renders it. The first fix named a deploy step, but the next check found no deploy method that fits every site. It also found that a hand-built site needs a pull, a build, and a deploy after the publish.

The page now checks through a share link on the dev server. The `(site)/preview/[token]` route renders the saved draft through the same `publicRoutesConfig` as the public entry pages. The dev backend serves `/preview` with the admin's in-memory backend and fake auth store, so the link resolves there. Two fresh checks traced each step, including the save, the mint, the origin, and the UI labels. Nothing gets published or deployed, and no test component lands on a live entry. A hand-built site needs the preview route and a `PUBLIC_ORIGIN`, and the lead-in says so.

sides.text: Keep the share-link check. It runs entirely on the dev server, and it shows the same markup the public page will. Publishing a test component to a live site to verify it costs more and needs site-specific deploy steps.
Check the published page itself, after a deploy. That's the end-to-end proof, at the cost of a deploy and a test entry on the live site.

choices.label: Keep the share-link check
choices.done: The page and blueprint stay as drafted.

choices.label: Restore the published-page check
choices.done: The session restores the publish-and-deploy steps, naming both deploy paths, then rechecks them.

anchor.quote: When the site's DaisyUI plugin config leaves a component enabled

title: The DaisyUI clash depends on the enabled set
body: The draft said DaisyUI styles any of its class names it finds in source. daisyUI 5.7.47 has an include and exclude filter (`index.js:18-29`), and the scaffold enables only badge, button, card, and alert. The page now says a reused name clashes only with a component the site leaves enabled.

anchor.quote: 'Announce a meeting, a workshop, or a talk.'

title: The example's text is neutral
body: The draft's `event` example announced a race and a bylaws vote, which lean toward the family's own sites. It now announces a meeting, a workshop, or a talk, with an annual report as the body. The output blocks were regenerated to match.

anchor.quote: Groups appear in the order first declared

title: Ungrouped components don't always lead
body: The draft said ungrouped components lead the picker. `groupDefs` places that group where its first member is declared (`ComponentInsertDialog.svelte:40-53`). The page and `f:rfeaa5` now say so, and this PR corrects the function's own comment, which made the same claim.

title: Stroke-only icons need a site rule
body: `renderGlyph` draws each path filled, with no stroke. The scaffold's own `snowflake` and `flag` icons are stroke-only, and `prose.css` adds a stroke to show them. The page now says a stroke-only path renders invisible unless the site's CSS adds a stroke.
